title: [3.x] AudioServer::Bus::index_cache is only assigned inside _mix_step(), so thread_find_bus_index() returns an uninitialized or stale bus index

milestone.title: 3.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 3 release.

body:
### Tested versions

Reproducible in 3.6.3-rc (`32115e784f`)
48 kHz mix rate, default 1024-frame mix buffer, default audio/output_latency = 15 ms


### System information

Linux (CachyOS, kernel 6.x), Godot 3.6.3-rc custom build with gcc version 16.1.1 20260625 (GCC) , GLES2 (Radeon 9070xt default linux drivers), Dummy audio driver,  64gb RAM

### Issue description

AudioServer::Bus::index_cache     (from servers/audio_server.h )  has no class initializer. only assignment to it is inside the mixer.

Every path that makes a Bus assigns name, solo, mute, bypass and volume_db, but never index_cache or soloed

This made my project fail about 15% of the time due to the random value of the uninitialized value (the built-in players resolve their target bus from a notification rather than the mixer)

The scripting API and the internal are also different because it figures out the index by scanning buses, so from gdscript the bus layout is correct yet the actual engine can still be using the stale cache

also when the check rejects the block, the code at scene/3d/audio_stream_player_3d.cpp:216 is also skipped so filter_process never gets the data for that block, which then goes interpolate_filter which ramps the values up, this means launching the same project multiple times, the sound mixing is randomly different for the first moment.

this is an example patch if you want to see it
[16-audio-server-bus-index-cache.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32099334/16-audio-server-bus-index-cache.patch)


### Steps to reproduce


To make it happen at runtime, create a bus and start a player on it during the the same frame while the engine is already running, so that the physics notification _might_ land before the next mix.

```
extends Node

const BLOCK = 1024

var probes = []
var master
var elapsed = 0.0
var started = false


func _ready():
	var camera = ClassDB.instance("Camera")
	add_child(camera)
	camera.call("make_current")
	get_viewport().set_as_audio_listener(true)


func _first_energy_block(capture):
	var buffer = capture.get_buffer(capture.get_frames_available())
	for b in range(int(buffer.size() / BLOCK)):
		var energy = 0.0
		for i in range(b * BLOCK, (b + 1) * BLOCK):
			energy += buffer[i].x * buffer[i].x + buffer[i].y * buffer[i].y
		if energy > 1e-9:
			return b
	return -1


func _process(delta):
	elapsed += delta
	# Create the buses and start the players within one frame, mid-run.
	if not started and elapsed >= 0.2:
		started = true
		master = AudioEffectCapture.new()
		master.buffer_length = 4.0
		AudioServer.add_bus_effect(0, master)
		var players = []
		for i in range(2):
			AudioServer.add_bus()
			var index = AudioServer.get_bus_count() - 1
			AudioServer.set_bus_name(index, "Probe%d" % i)
			var capture = AudioEffectCapture.new()
			capture.buffer_length = 4.0
			AudioServer.add_bus_effect(index, capture)
			probes.append(capture)
		for i in range(2):
			var player = ClassDB.instance("AudioStreamPlayer3D")
			add_child(player)
			player.bus = "Probe%d" % i
			player.unit_size = 1.0
			player.translation = Vector3(0.0, 0.0, -1.0)
			player.stream = load("res://tone.wav")
			players.append(player)
		for player in players:
			player.play()
		return
	if not started or elapsed < 0.6:
		return
	print("master_first_block=%d probe0_first_block=%d probe1_first_block=%d"
			% [_first_energy_block(master), _first_energy_block(probes[0]), _first_energy_block(probes[1])])
	get_tree().quit()
```
If you run it repeatedly then it will trigger. On a good run the bus probe catches it, on a bad run the master catches the start of it and the probe only gets the 2nd or 3rd block and misses the beginning. This is how I found it because I was making a custom audio player and the unit tests would randomly fail sometimes but still work most of the time so I find out why it was flaky

Note: that creating the buses in _ready() instead does not reproduce it because a mix step reliably intervenes before the first physics tick. It has to be ones spawned while the engine is already running.





### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Attached a blank GLES2 project containing the script a generated wav and a Camera. Run it repeatedly from the command line
(I use --audio-driver Dummy) and count the lines where master_first_block is lower than the probe. In theory they should all be the same but it depends on ram contents of the uninitialized var.

[godot-bus-index-cache-repro.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32099323/godot-bus-index-cache-repro.zip)
